changes.item: AC-2 wording: 'lower is refused' contradicted 'may re-learn more, never less'
changes.before: a client value lower than the server's k is refused (closed code), higher is accepted (the author may choose to re-learn more, never less);
changes.after: a client `firstLearnStepId` positioned after the server's k in the current draft (it would skip a changed or drifted step) is refused with `409 REVISION_CONFLICT` and `messageCode` `FIRST_LEARN_STEP_NARROWED`, and one at or before k is accepted (the author may choose to re-learn more, never less); position is the step ID's index in the current draft authoring, never the UUID value;
changes.reason: As written, 'lower' read as an earlier step means more re-learning, which the parenthetical allows. Step UUIDs have no order. The ruling fixes the invariant (never later than k, compared by draft position) and names the refusal. Meaning per the ruling ('no meaning change intended').

changes.before: client `firstLearnStepId` lower than server k ⇒ refused;
changes.after: client `firstLearnStepId` positioned after the server's k ⇒ `409 REVISION_CONFLICT`, `messageCode` `FIRST_LEARN_STEP_NARROWED`;
changes.reason: Same contradiction; the oracle must name the ruled refusal before T5 writes it.

changes.before: a test-level configuration change (environment, approved origins, viewport, timeout, browser) ⇒ k = 1;
changes.after: a test-level configuration change (environment, which selects the approved origins; viewport, timeout, browser) ⇒ k = 1, while a governed-policy or `TrustedPolicy` change never changes k;
changes.reason: After OBS-014, origins come from the governed or trusted policy, not the draft. They enter change detection only through environment, and a governance change never changes k (consistent with AR-2 g).
